# Status

**This script has not been run.** It was drafted against the real sample sheet and the
real file names, and its design matrices were checked for rank deficiency, but the count
data do not exist yet: quantification must be done first with
`Code/07-AAC-RNAseq_quantification.sh` on a machine that can hold 41 GB of reads and
build a salmon index. Treat every numeric claim below as a placeholder until the knit
produces it.

# Design

34 libraries, all *Pocillopora meandrina*, **single-end**, each sequenced twice. The two
runs per library are technical replicates and are concatenated upstream; they must never
enter the model as separate samples.

| | held at Opunohu | held at Tiahura | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-HS (F60) | 10 | 10 | 20 |
| Post-HS (F80) | 5 | 9 | 14 |

Pre-HS is complete: all 10 colonies contributed a fragment at each bay. Post-HS is not -
six fragments are missing, and **the loss is not random with respect to bay**: only 5 of
14 post-heat-shock libraries come from fragments held at Opunohu, against 9 from Tiahura.
Any `Destination` or `Destination:Timepoint` effect is therefore confounded to some degree
with whatever caused fragments at the impacted bay to drop out, which may well be
mortality. This is the single most important caveat in the script and it cannot be fixed
analytically.

Origin is a property of the colony; destination and timepoint vary within a colony. All
four candidate designs are full rank on this sample sheet:

| Design | Model columns | Residual df |
|---|---|---|
| `~ Colony_ID + Destination * Timepoint` | 13 | 21 |
| `~ Colony_ID + Timepoint` | 11 | 23 |
| `~ Origin + Destination * Timepoint` | 5 | 29 |
| `~ Destination * Timepoint` | 4 | 30 |

The **colony-blocked design is used by default**: it absorbs genotype, which the 16S and
ITS2 analyses both showed to be a strong structuring factor, and 21 residual df is ample
for DESeq2's dispersion estimation. `~ Origin + Destination * Timepoint` is kept as a
fallback if colony blocking proves too costly on this sample size.

# Prepare workspace

```{r libraries}
library(DESeq2)
library(tximport)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(tibble)
library(vegan)    # betadisper, for the expression-space dispersion test in section 6

dir_out_dat <- file.path("..", "..", "Data",    "07-AAC-RNAseq")
dir_out_fig <- file.path("..", "..", "Figures", "07-AAC-RNAseq")
dir_out_tab <- file.path("..", "..", "Tables",  "07-AAC-RNAseq")
pref_out    <- "07-AAC-RNAseq_"
for (d in c(dir_out_dat, dir_out_fig, dir_out_tab)) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

alpha_fdr <- 0.05     # adjusted-p threshold used throughout
lfc_min   <- 1        # |log2FC| threshold for "responsive" gene counts

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA)))
col_tp <- c("Pre-HS" = "#4C72B0", "Post-HS" = "#C44E52")
```

# Import counts

```{r import-samples}
samples <- read.csv(file.path(dir_out_dat, paste0(pref_out, "samples.csv")),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Timepoint   = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Pre-HS", "Post-HS")),
    Destination = factor(Destination, levels = c("Opunohu", "Tiahura")),
    Origin      = factor(Origin,      levels = c("Opunohu", "Tiahura")),
    Colony_ID   = factor(Colony_ID))
rownames(samples) <- samples$Sample_ID

stopifnot(nrow(samples) == 34, nlevels(samples$Colony_ID) == 10)
print(table(samples$Destination, samples$Timepoint))
```

```{r import-tximport}
files <- file.path(dir_out_dat, "salmon", samples$Sample_ID, "quant.sf")
names(files) <- samples$Sample_ID
stopifnot(all(file.exists(files)))

tx2gene <- read.delim(file.path(dir_out_dat, "tx2gene.tsv"),
                      header = FALSE, col.names = c("TXNAME", "GENEID"))

# countsFromAbundance = "lengthScaledTPM" gives DESeq2 counts that are already
# corrected for transcript length and library size composition; the alternative
# (type = "salmon" with an offset) is equivalent but less portable downstream.
txi <- tximport::tximport(files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene,
                          countsFromAbundance = "lengthScaledTPM")

cat("genes:", nrow(txi$counts), "| samples:", ncol(txi$counts), "\n")
```

# Quality control

```{r qc-mapping}
# Host mapping rate is QC and biology at once: reads that fail to map are largely
# Cladocopium, so a drop in host mapping rate means a rise in the symbiont fraction.
# Test it explicitly before dismissing it as technical noise.
mapping <- read.delim(file.path(dir_out_dat, "mapping_rates.tsv")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(samples, Sample_ID, Timepoint, Destination, Colony_ID),
                   by = "Sample_ID")

mapping |>
  dplyr::group_by(Timepoint) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                   median_pct_mapped = round(median(percent_mapped), 2),
                   median_reads = median(num_processed), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Host mapping rate by timepoint")

wt <- wilcox.test(percent_mapped ~ Timepoint, data = mapping)
cat("Mann-Whitney on host mapping rate, Pre-HS vs Post-HS: p =",
    signif(wt$p.value, 3), "\n")

plot_MappingRate <- ggplot(mapping, aes(Timepoint, percent_mapped,
                                        colour = Timepoint, fill = Timepoint)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.3, width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.13, size = 2.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ Destination, labeller = labeller(Destination = function(x) paste("held at", x))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_tp) + scale_fill_manual(values = col_tp) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "reads mapped to P. meandrina (%)",
       title = "Host mapping rate as a proxy for symbiont fraction")
ggsave(file.path(dir_out_fig, paste0(pref_out, "plot_MappingRate.png")),
       plot_MappingRate, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
plot_MappingRate
```

```{r build-dds}
dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi, colData = samples,
                                        design = ~ Colony_ID + Destination * Timepoint)

# Independent filtering: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least as many
# samples as the smallest group (5 = Post-HS at Opunohu).
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 5
cat("genes retained:", sum(keep), "of", nrow(dds), "\n")
dds <- dds[keep, ]

vsd <- DESeq2::vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
```

```{r qc-pca}
pca_dat <- DESeq2::plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("Timepoint", "Destination"),
                           returnData = TRUE)
pct <- round(100 * attr(pca_dat, "percentVar"))

plot_PCA <- ggplot(pca_dat, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Timepoint, shape = Destination)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_tp) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pct[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", pct[2], "%)"),
       shape = "Held at", title = "Variance-stabilised expression, all retained genes")
ggsave(file.path(dir_out_fig, paste0(pref_out, "plot_PCA.png")),
       plot_PCA, width = 6.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
plot_PCA
```

```{r qc-sample-distances}
sampleDists <- dist(t(assay(vsd)))
mat <- as.matrix(sampleDists)
rownames(mat) <- paste(vsd$Timepoint, vsd$Destination, vsd$Colony_ID, sep = " | ")
colnames(mat) <- NULL
png(file.path(dir_out_fig, paste0(pref_out, "plot_SampleDistances.png")),
    width = 9, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
pheatmap::pheatmap(mat, clustering_distance_rows = sampleDists,
                   clustering_distance_cols = sampleDists,
                   col = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "Blues")))(255),
                   main = "Euclidean distance between samples (vst)")
dev.off()
pheatmap::pheatmap(mat, clustering_distance_rows = sampleDists,
                   clustering_distance_cols = sampleDists,
                   col = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "Blues")))(255))
```

# Differential expression

```{r deseq-fit}
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)
```

```{r deseq-interaction}
# Is the heat-shock response bay-dependent? Tested by LRT against the additive model,
# which is the correct test for the interaction as a whole rather than one coefficient.
dds_lrt <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, test = "LRT",
                         reduced = ~ Colony_ID + Destination + Timepoint)
res_int  <- DESeq2::results(dds_lrt, alpha = alpha_fdr)
cat("genes with a bay-dependent heat-shock response (FDR <", alpha_fdr, "):",
    sum(res_int$padj < alpha_fdr, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
summary(res_int)
```

```{r deseq-contrasts}
# With an interaction in the model, the `Timepoint` coefficient is the heat-shock effect
# AT THE REFERENCE DESTINATION (Opunohu), not an average. Extract each bay explicitly.
res_hs_opunohu <- DESeq2::results(dds, name = "Timepoint_Post.HS_vs_Pre.HS",
                                  alpha = alpha_fdr)
res_hs_tiahura <- DESeq2::results(dds, alpha = alpha_fdr,
                                  contrast = list(c("Timepoint_Post.HS_vs_Pre.HS",
                                                    "DestinationTiahura.TimepointPost.HS")))

# apeglm cannot shrink arbitrary contrasts; ashr can, so use it throughout for
# comparability between the two bays.
res_hs_opunohu <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(dds, res = res_hs_opunohu, type = "ashr")
res_hs_tiahura <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(dds, res = res_hs_tiahura, type = "ashr")

tab_de <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(Contrast = "Heat shock, fragments held at Opunohu",
             n_up   = sum(res_hs_opunohu$padj < alpha_fdr & res_hs_opunohu$log2FoldChange >  lfc_min, na.rm = TRUE),
             n_down = sum(res_hs_opunohu$padj < alpha_fdr & res_hs_opunohu$log2FoldChange < -lfc_min, na.rm = TRUE)),
  data.frame(Contrast = "Heat shock, fragments held at Tiahura",
             n_up   = sum(res_hs_tiahura$padj < alpha_fdr & res_hs_tiahura$log2FoldChange >  lfc_min, na.rm = TRUE),
             n_down = sum(res_hs_tiahura$padj < alpha_fdr & res_hs_tiahura$log2FoldChange < -lfc_min, na.rm = TRUE)),
  data.frame(Contrast = "Bay-dependent heat-shock response (LRT)",
             n_up = sum(res_int$padj < alpha_fdr, na.rm = TRUE), n_down = NA_integer_))
knitr::kable(tab_de, caption = paste0("Differentially expressed genes (FDR < ",
                                      alpha_fdr, ", |log2FC| > ", lfc_min, ")"))

write.csv(as.data.frame(res_hs_opunohu) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID"),
          file.path(dir_out_tab, paste0(pref_out, "DE_HeatShock_Opunohu.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame(res_hs_tiahura) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID"),
          file.path(dir_out_tab, paste0(pref_out, "DE_HeatShock_Tiahura.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame(res_int) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID"),
          file.path(dir_out_tab, paste0(pref_out, "DE_Interaction_LRT.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-volcano}
volc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(res_hs_opunohu) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(Bay = "held at Opunohu"),
  as.data.frame(res_hs_tiahura) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(Bay = "held at Tiahura")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Significant = padj < alpha_fdr & abs(log2FoldChange) > lfc_min)

plot_Volcano <- ggplot(volc, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), colour = Significant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(alpha_fdr), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_min, lfc_min), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~ Bay) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#C44E52")) +
  labs(x = expression(log[2]~fold~change~("Post-HS vs Pre-HS")),
       y = expression(-log[10]~adjusted~p),
       title = "Host transcriptional response to acute heat shock")
ggsave(file.path(dir_out_fig, paste0(pref_out, "plot_Volcano.png")),
       plot_Volcano, width = 8.5, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
plot_Volcano
```

```{r fig-topgenes}
top_genes <- as.data.frame(res_hs_tiahura) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("GeneID") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 40) |>
  dplyr::pull(GeneID)

if (length(top_genes) > 1) {
  ann <- as.data.frame(colData(vsd)[, c("Timepoint", "Destination")])
  png(file.path(dir_out_fig, paste0(pref_out, "plot_TopGeneHeatmap.png")),
      width = 9, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
  pheatmap::pheatmap(assay(vsd)[top_genes, ], scale = "row",
                     annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE,
                     main = "Top 40 heat-shock-responsive genes (vst, row-scaled)")
  dev.off()
}
```

# Linking to the symbiont result

The ITS2 analysis (script 06) found that acute heat shock **did not shift the mean
Symbiodiniaceae community but increased among-fragment variability about 1.75-fold** in
this same host, with no equivalent destabilisation of the bacterial community. Two
questions follow directly and both are answerable from these data:

1. **Did the fragments actually experience thermal stress?** The ITS2 interpretation rests
   on treatment rather than measured stress. Induction of the canonical heat-shock
   machinery - HSP70/HSP90 chaperones, oxidative-stress and apoptosis regulators - would
   substantiate it; their absence would undermine it.
2. **Does host transcriptional variance also increase?** If heat shock destabilises the
   holobiont generally, among-fragment dispersion should rise in expression space too.
   This is a dispersion question, not a mean-shift question, so test it the same way the
   symbiont data were tested rather than reading it off the PCA.

```{r dispersion-in-expression-space}
# Among-sample dispersion in expression space, Pre-HS vs Post-HS - the direct analogue
# of the betadisper test used on the ITS2 data in script 06.
d_expr <- dist(t(assay(vsd)))
bd_expr <- vegan::betadisper(d_expr, vsd$Timepoint)
set.seed(42)
print(vegan::permutest(bd_expr, permutations = 999))
cat("\nratio of mean distance-to-centroid, Post-HS / Pre-HS: ",
    round(mean(bd_expr$distances[vsd$Timepoint == "Post-HS"]) /
          mean(bd_expr$distances[vsd$Timepoint == "Pre-HS"]), 2), "\n")
```

# Caveats

* **Post-heat-shock loss is bay-biased** (5 Opunohu against 9 Tiahura), so destination and
  interaction terms carry survivorship confounding that no model can remove. State it
  wherever those terms are reported.
* Reads are **single-end**, so `--gcBias` correction is unavailable and transcript-level
  inference is weaker than it would be with paired reads; gene-level aggregation via
  `tximport` mitigates this and is the reason the analysis is run at gene level.
* The PMEA_v1 assembly is **contig-level** (252 contigs) with a Genoscope annotation of
  32,095 protein-coding genes and **no GO or KEGG mapping**. Functional enrichment
  therefore needs an orthology step first (eggNOG-mapper or InterProScan against the
  provided protein fasta); the ranked tables exported above are the input for it.
* Reads not mapping to the host are predominantly *Cladocopium*. They are discarded here
  by the decoy-aware index, but the mapping rate is retained as a symbiont-fraction proxy
  and tested above - it is not merely a QC number in a holobiont.
* The two sequencing runs per library are concatenated upstream. If they are ever treated
  as separate samples the design inflates to 68 and every p-value is wrong.
